\ud83d\ude2d✨ Naisip mo na ba kung paano gawing isang malalim at emosyonal na “cry face” cinematic moment ang iyong ordinaryong portrait? Ang viral na AI photo trend na ito ay kayang gawing realistic emotional close-up portrait ang simpleng selfie mo, na puno ng luha, damdamin, at storytelling vibes \ud83c\udf9e️\ud83d\udc94. Ang AI effect na ito ay maaaring gawing isang sad but beautiful emotional portrait style ang iyong normal na selfie \ud83d\udcf8.

Panatilihing pareho ang tunay kong facial identity, natural na skin texture, natatanging facial features, at original na expression, habang nagdaragdag ng realistic na watery eyes, maliliit na luha, emotional gaze, at isang touching cinematic atmosphere. Huwag baguhin ang hugis ng mukha, mga personal na facial features, at natural na beauty; magdagdag lamang ng banayad na luha sa mga mata, soft emotion, at realistic feelings \ud83e\udd79✨.

Isipin mo ang sarili mo na parang nasa isang dramatic movie scene — teary eyes, gentle smile, soft shadows, emotional lighting, at isang makapangyarihang tahimik na kuwento sa likod ng iyong mukha \ud83c\udfac. Pinagsasama ng style na ito ang sadness at beauty upang makalikha ng feeling na parang isa kang tunay na movie character \ud83c\udf19.

Gumawa ng realistic na background na parang isang heartbreaking ngunit magandang alaala: warm indoor lights, reflections ng ulan sa bintana, blurred city atmosphere, tahimik na kuwarto, soft cinematic background, at emotional movie vibes \ud83c\udf27️✨. Dapat magmukhang frame mula sa isang romantic drama film o isang unforgettable emotional scene ang iyong larawan.

Para gawin ang viral AI “cry face” trend na ito gamit ang ChatGPT o Gemini AI, i-upload ang malinaw mong portrait photo at gamitin ang prompt na ito:

“Keep my face identity, facial features, skin tone and natural expression unchanged. Transform my portrait into a realistic emotional cry face cinematic photograph with watery eyes, subtle tears, soft emotional expression, realistic skin texture, dramatic lighting, movie scene atmosphere and high-detail portrait photography.”

Idagdag ang mga AI keywords na ito: “crying face portrait, emotional eyes, realistic tears, cinematic close-up, sad beauty aesthetic, dramatic portrait photography, soft film lighting, emotional movie scene, realistic skin details, shallow depth of field, ultra realistic photography” \ud83d\udcf7\ud83d\udca7.

Sa ganitong cry face AI effect, mahalaga ang realistic tears, emotional eyes, soft lighting, at cinematic mood. Dahil dito, hindi ito basta mukhang AI-generated image, kundi parang isang emotional moment mula mismo sa isang tunay na film scene \ud83e\udd7a\ud83c\udf9e️.

Gawing isang powerful emotional memory ang iyong simpleng larawan — isang kuwentong kayang sabihin nang walang salita \ud83d\udc96. I-share ang iyong cry face transformation sa TikTok, Instagram, o iba pang social media at hayaan ang lahat na maramdaman ang emotion sa likod ng iyong mga mata ✨.

The number π is an irrational number, meaning that it cannot be expressed exactly as a ratio of two integers, although fractions such as ⁠

⁠ are commonly used to approximate it. Consequently, its decimal representation never ends, nor does it enter a permanently repeating pattern. It is a transcendental number, meaning that it cannot be a solution of an algebraic equation involving only finite sums, products, powers, and integers. The transcendence of π implies that it is impossible to solve the ancient problem of squaring the circle with a compass and straightedge. The decimal digits of π appear to be evenly distributed, but no proof of this conjecture has been found.

Mathematicians have attempted to extend their understanding of π, sometimes by computing its value to a high degree of accuracy. Ancient civilizations, including the Egyptians and Babylonians, required fairly accurate approximations of π for practical computations. Around 250 BC, the Greek mathematician Archimedes created an algorithm to approximate π with arbitrary accuracy. In the 5th century AD, Chinese mathematicians approximated π to seven digits, while Indian mathematicians made a five-digit approximation, both using geometrical techniques. The first computational formula for π, based on infinite series, was discovered a millennium later.

The earliest known use of the Greek letter π to represent the ratio of a circle's circumference to its diameter was by the Welsh mathematician William Jones in 1706. The invention of calculus soon led to the calculation of hundreds of digits of π, enough for all practical scientific computations. Nevertheless, in the 20th and 21st centuries, mathematicians and computer scientists have pursued new approaches that, when combined with increasing computational power, extended the decimal representation of π to hundreds of trillions of digits. These computations are motivated by the development of efficient algorithms to calculate numeric series, as well as the human quest to break records. The extensive computations involved have also been used to test the correctness of new computer processors.

Because it relates to a circle, π is found in formulae in trigonometry and geometry, especially those concerning circles, ellipses and spheres. It is found as well in formulae from cosmology, fractals, thermodynamics, mechanics, and electromagnetism. snapshot1Rescored.author: bdinvesting
snapshot1Rescored.caption:
\ud83c\udde8\ud83c\udde6 Canadian business owners could soon get a much bigger tax write-off.

Canada has proposed the Productivity Mega Deduction, which would let businesses immediately deduct 100% of the cost of most eligible depreciable business assets through CCA once they’re available for use, instead of depreciating them over several years. The proposal generally applies to eligible property acquired on or after September 15, 2026. 

That could include things like:

\ud83d\udcbb Computers \u0026 MacBooks
\ud83d\udcf1 Eligible business phones/devices
⚙️ Machinery, equipment \u0026 tools
\ud83d\udda5️ Technology \u0026 data equipment
\ud83d\udd2c Certain R\u0026D equipment

The important part: personal use vs. business use matters.

If you buy a $2,000 phone and reasonably use it:

• 100% for business → up to $2,000 could potentially form the eligible business claim
• 80% business / 20% personal → about $1,600 business portion
• 50% business / 50% personal → about $1,000 business portion

CRA says personal expenses aren’t deductible, and when a cellphone is used for both business and personal purposes, you need a reasonable method of determining the business-use portion. 

The same principle applies to your monthly phone plan. If a $100/month plan is 70% reasonably attributable to business, roughly $70/month would generally be the business expense rather than automatically claiming the full $100. 

⚠️ This does not mean everyone can buy an iPhone and automatically write off 100%. The asset still needs to qualify under the CCA rules, the business-use percentage needs to be supportable, and the Productivity Mega Deduction is currently proposed legislation, not yet enacted. 

Educational purposes only — not tax advice. Check with your accountant/CPA for your situation.

snapshot1Rescored.caption:
When your lender says, “She NEEDS a seller credit for closing costs…” and then the contract shows up with exactly $0 in seller credits. \ud83d\ude2d\ud83d\ude02

This is why your mortgage lender and real estate agent need to communicate BEFORE the offer is written.

For some homebuyers, having enough money for the down payment doesn’t automatically mean they have enough to cover closing costs, prepaid taxes, homeowners insurance, and other cash-to-close expenses.

So if your pre-approval is structured around receiving a seller credit toward closing costs, that credit needs to actually make it into the contract. \ud83d\udc40

Can we sometimes restructure things afterward? Maybe.

But depending on the buyer’s available funds, loan program, purchase price, and debt-to-income ratio, leaving out that seller concession could completely change the numbers—or even create a problem with qualifying.

Moral of the story: if the lender says the buyer needs something written into the offer… please believe us. \ud83d\ude02

And buyers: this is exactly why having a lender and Realtor who actually communicate with each other matters.

\ud83c\udfe1 Thinking about buying a home? Get pre-approved before you start writing offers so you know exactly how much cash you’ll need and how your offer should be structured.
